pick.headline: Cuba shoots down Brothers to the Rescue planes
pick.summary: On February 24, 1996, Cuban MiGs shot down two civilian planes of the Miami exile group Brothers to the Rescue, killing four men.
pick.significance: Havana had been forewarned by a Cuban agent inside the group. The shootdown led Clinton to sign the Helms-Burton Act tightening the embargo.
pick.fbis: The Latin America Daily Report of February 26, 1996, opened its Cuba section with Paris AFP from Miami and Havana: anti-Castro sources confirmed Cuban MiGs downed two Brothers to the Rescue planes, Cuba's Foreign Ministry had no information "so far", and exile groups named the crew.

alternates.headline: Coalition ground offensive begins
alternates.summary: On February 24, 1991, coalition forces began the ground offensive against Iraqi forces in Kuwait and southern Iraq.
alternates.significance: Within 100 hours Iraq's army was routed and Kuwait liberated.
